problem: Embodied RL agents suffer from scarce, sparse-reward data. Prior hindsight relabeling and diffusion augmentation methods need human labels for tasks, or are not geometrically/temporally consistent, so they cannot reuse trajectories that fail the current task.
motivation: Lifelong agents need to reuse past experience for new tasks without human supervision. Failed or off-task episodes contain useful visual and action structure, and foundation models can relabel and edit them autonomously.
key_idea: An LLM orchestrates a VLM and a geometry- and temporally-consistent diffusion pipeline (ControlNet + Text2Video-Zero style) to edit past observations so old episodes appear to solve the new task (Hindsight Experience Augmentation), giving synthetic reward-detector data and RL training data.
insight: Diffusion-edited observations paired with the original actions give usable successful demonstrations only if object geometry and pose stay consistent across frames. This lets agents get signal from episodes that never solved the target task. Results show a fine-tuned CLIP detects a task with zero real examples, where zero-shot CLIP is near random on RGB Stacking and Language Table. A RetinaGAN-like baseline needs about 100 real examples of the new task to learn its mapping, whereas DAAG works zero-shot. All results are shown in figures only, with no tables.
method: LLM controller (Gemini Pro 1.0): decomposes tasks into subgoals, compares task captions to decide whether an object swap turns one into another (two-stage prompt: propose swap, then re-verify), and queries the diffusion model.

VLM reward detector (CLIP ViT-B/32): fine-tuned on real and synthetic goal observations; labels an observation as achieving a subgoal if cosine similarity exceeds a threshold δ chosen on held-out validation data.

Consistent diffusion pipeline: Stable Diffusion 1.5 inpainting of a source object into a target object (localized via OWL-ViT plus FastSAM/CLIPSeg), with ControlNets on Canny, depth (MiDaS) and normals for geometric consistency; fixed initial noise plus cross-frame attention (Text2Video-Zero) for temporal consistency.

Hindsight Experience Augmentation (HEA): for an episode that achieved subgoal X but not the desired one, the LLM finds a swap; the diffusion model edits observations up to the achieved subgoal, and (edited obs, original actions) are added to the new-task buffer.

Lifelong buffer and transfer: all episodes are stored in B_ll; on a new task HEA is applied to the whole buffer to seed B_n, a policy is pre-trained, and HEA is then applied to new exploration episodes.
Policy learning: self-imitation behaviour cloning (ResNet-18 + 2-layer MLP) on successful or relabeled episodes in B_n, with epsilon-greedy exploration.
Scene visual augmentation: the same pipeline changes backgrounds (floor/walls) to make policies robust to visual changes.

setting.backbone: Gemini Pro 1.0 (frozen LLM) + CLIP ViT-B/32 (fine-tuned) + Stable Diffusion 1.5 with ControlNet (frozen) + ResNet-18/MLP policy (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Self-collected episodes in each simulated environment: 100 goal observations per task for CLIP fine-tuning, 200 offline episodes per task for transfer, plus diffusion-synthesized observations
setting.observation: monocular RGB (fixed shoulder camera for RGB Stacking and Language Table; first-person camera for Room)
setting.action_space: pick-and-place positions (RGB Stacking); forward and rotational velocity (Room); end-effector xy velocity (Language Table)
setting.simulator: Custom environments: RGB Stacking, Room, Language Table

numbers_note: All results are only in figures (bar and learning-curve plots); the paper reports no numeric tables. Navigation is only a custom Room environment, not a standard benchmark.
results: Fine-tuned CLIP with diffusion-synthesized data detects rewards for an unseen task, beating zero-shot CLIP and CLIP fine-tuned on other tasks in all three environments. DAAG learns new tasks faster than the Di Palo et al. 2023 subgoal-decomposition baseline and a goal-conditioned policy baseline, both when exploring and when transferring past experience. It also gives forward and backward transfer and more robust policies via scene augmentation.
limitations: Only simple simulated environments with object-swap edits and a fixed set of three tasks. There are no real-robot or standard navigation benchmark results, and results are qualitative in figures with 3 seeds.
Assumes that replaying original actions on edited observations solves the new task, which requires geometric consistency; only relatively simple color or object swaps are handled.
Depends on a pipeline of many off-the-shelf models (Gemini, CLIP, SD, OWL-ViT, SAM), and CLIP needs fine-tuning because it is near random zero-shot.
builds_on: Di Palo et al. 2023 (Towards a Unified Agent)
compares_to: Di Palo et al. 2023 unified agent (subgoal decomposition)
